passage:
Saturday: At the new neighbour's door, Sharmila gave Minakshi a small smile with her lips pressed together and stayed half behind her mother. “Hi!” said Minakshi. Sharmila nodded. Her mother did not say “smile properly”.
Tuesday: Minakshi waved at the lift. Sharmila's smile was the same size, but this time she said “hi” in a soft voice.
Sunday: on the compound steps with a football between them, Sharmila laughed with teeth showing. “Your turn,” she said.

qa.q: What did Sharmila do at the neighbour's door on Saturday?
qa.a: She gave Minakshi a small smile with her lips pressed together and stayed half behind her mother.

qa.q: What was Sharmila most likely feeling on Saturday, and what else might it be?
qa.a: Most likely shy with someone new, since she stayed half behind her mother and only nodded. It could also be politeness with some caution; the size of a smile does not show how much she liked Minakshi.
She did not tell Sharmila to smile bigger, which gave her time to warm up in her own way.

qa.q: How might Minakshi have read the small smile on Saturday?
qa.a: She might have thought Sharmila was unfriendly, or she might have sensed shyness. She kept greeting her anyway, which helped.

grounding: A closed-mouth smile with new people is shyness or politeness; time and no forcing respect temperament.

passage:
“Listen, Aditi,” said Ishita Nani, stirring her tea. “You were nine when we went to your cousin's wedding in Jaipur. So many new faces! You gave everyone the same small smile with your lips closed and held on to my dupatta. Your mother whispered, ‘Smile properly!’ and I said, ‘Leave her, she is looking first.’ An hour later you were the one telling the little cousins how to play the game with marbles. You did not need a bigger smile. You needed time.”
Aditi grinned. “I still do that.”
“I know, beta.”

qa.q: How old was Aditi when they went to the wedding in Jaipur?
What did Ishita Nani think Aditi's small smile meant?
qa.a: That Aditi was shy and taking in many new faces, not unhappy or rude. She said Aditi was “looking first”, though she does not claim to know for certain.

qa.q: What did Ishita do that helped Aditi at the wedding?
qa.a: She told Aditi's mother to leave her alone, giving Aditi time to watch and warm up, and an hour later she was leading a game.

qa.q: How might Aditi's mother have felt when she whispered “Smile properly!”?
qa.a: Perhaps a little embarrassed that relatives would think Aditi impolite. Nani's answer shows a different way to see the smile.

grounding: A closed-mouth smile with new people carries shyness; giving time respects temperament.
